message.content: In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is regarded as the most significant figure and is often referred to as the ultimate prophet, the Son of God, and the Savior. While other prophets such as Moses, Isaiah, and John the Baptist hold important roles—Moses as the lawgiver, Isaiah as a major prophet of the Old Testament, and John the Baptist as the forerunner who prepared the way for Jesus—Christian tradition places Jesus at the center of faith. He is seen as fulfilling the prophecies of the Old Testament and establishing the New Covenant, making him the focal point of Christian belief and worship.
